correctness.rationale: For every rooted out-arborescence the only changed indegree is that of the new target. The non-target descendants receive one common trophic-level shift, so every old link except the original parent edge of the target keeps trophic difference 1. For an acyclic chord, solving s(v)=1+(s(parent)+s(u))/2 yields deviations ±(d(v)-d(u)-1)/2, hence q²=(d(v)-d(u)-1)²/(2n). If the source is a descendant, its shifted level enters its own target equation, giving deviations ±(ell+1), hence q²=2(ell+1)²/n. The basal root remains fixed and the linear system has a unique solution in both cases. The sharp feedback gap, acyclic minimum and zero-cost count ∑ a_h(a_(h-1)-1) follow with no omitted source-target cases. A separate rational direct solution checks 1,602 allowed additions across all rooted labelled trees on 3,4,5 vertices (144 rooted trees) and 144 zero counts; finite work is corroboration, not the unbounded proof.

value.rationale: Trophic incoherence is a motivated food-web hierarchy invariant tied to feedback structure. The theorem gives an exact edge-insertion cost independent of branching topology, a sharp feedback-versus-acyclic separation, and a complete coherence-preserving link enumeration. These are substantive universal structural assertions, not recitations of the metric definition or arbitrary small examples.
